A number of metrics is employed in the field of aquaculture in order to describe aspects such as the growth or feed conversion in a comparable manner. This vignette provides a formulary and expands the background on the metrics that have been implemented in the aquacultuR package.



# Overview

|Trivial                                          |Abbrev.  |Synonyms   |Symbol               |SI unit|
|-------------------------------------------------|---------|-----------|---------------------|-------|
|Absolute growth                                  |AG       |weight gain|$\Delta m$      |g
|Absolute growth rate                             |AGR      |           |$r_{\text{AG}}$      |g/d
|Apparent Digestibility Coefficient               |ADC      |           |
|Apparent Digestibility Coefficient - Dry Matter  |ADC-DM   |           |
|Apparent Digestibility Coefficient - Nutrient    |ADC-Nut  |           |
|Apparent Digestibility Coefficient - Ingredient  |ADC-Ingr |           |
|Body weight                                      |BW       |           |$m_{\text{BW}}$      |g
|Feed conversion ratio                            |FCR      |           |$m_{f}:m_{\text{AG}}$|g/g
|Feed efficiency ratio                            |FER      |           |$m_{\text{AG}}:m_{f}$|g/g
|Feed fed                                         |Ff       |           |$r_{\text{Ff}}$      |g/d
|Feed intake                                      |FI       |           |$r_{\text{FI}}$      |g/d
|Feeding rate                                     |FR       |           |$r_{\text{FR}}$      |g/m d
|Final body weight                                |FBW      |           |$m_{\text{end}}$     |g
|Geometric body weight                            |GBW      |           |$m_{geom}$           |g
|Initial body weight                              |IBW      |           |$m_{\text{init}}$    |g
|Metabolic body weight                            |MBW      |           |$m_{\text{MBW}}$     |g
|Relative growth rate                             |RGR      |           |$r_{\text{RGR}}$
|Specific growth rate                             |SGR      |           |
|Thermal growth coefficient                       |TGC      |           |



|Parameter                  |Abbrev.    |Symbol     |SI unit|
|---------------------------|-----------|-----------|-------|
|Time                       |           |$t$        |d
|Temperature                |temp       |$T$        |°C





# Alphabetic Formulary

## Absolute Growth

$$
\Delta m
  = m_{\text{end}} - m_{\text{init}} 
$$




## Absolute Growth Rate

- average growth rate

$$
\text{AGR} 
  = \frac{\Delta m}{\Delta t}
$$



## Apparent Digestibility Coefficient - Dry Matter

$$
\text{ADC}_{\text{DM}} = 
  1 - (\frac{\gamma_{feed}}{\gamma_{feces}})
$$


## Apparent Digestibility Coefficient - Nutrient

$$
\text{ADC}_{\text{x}} = 
  1 - (\frac{\gamma_{std, feed}} {\gamma_{std,feces}} \cdot \frac{\gamma_{x,feces}}{\gamma_{x, feed}})
$$


## Apparent Digestibility Coefficient - Ingredient

$$
\text{ADC}_{ingr} = ADC_{test} + (ADC_{test} - ADC_{ref}) \cdot (\frac{f_{ref} \cdot \gamma_{x,ref}}{f_{ingredient} \cdot \gamma_{x, ingredient}})
$$


## Feed Conversion Efficiency

The Feed Conversion Efficiency (FCE) is the inverse of the Feed Conversion Ratio (FCR). 

$$
\text{FCE} 
  = \frac{1}{\text{FCR}} 
  = \frac{\Delta m}{\text{FI} \cdot \text{DM}}
$$


## Feed Conversion Ratio
The Feed Conversion Ratio (FCR) is one of the most commonly used metrics in the field of animal production and animal nutrition, as it provides a simple way of relating the quantity of feed administered to achieve a certain increase in biomass. Several versions of the FCR are used in literature. After correction for the true dry matter ($DM$) content of the feed, which makes FCRs comparable, the two most common FCRs are the $eFCR$ (economic FCR) and the $bFCR$ (biological FCR) (Glencross et al., 2024).

The $eFCR$ takes the amount of feed fed ($Ff$) into consideration for the computation of the result. This is more meaningful in a business setup, because the $eFCR$ would also respond to, for instance, changes in the feeding strategy that might lead to a decrease in feed loss.

$$
\text{eFCR}
  = \frac{\text{Ff} \cdot \text{DM}}{\Delta m}
$$



The $bFCR$, meanwhile, only considers the true feed intake ($FI$), which is the amount of feed fed, but corrected for feed refusal or feed losses. 

$$
\text{bFCR}
  = \frac{\text{FI} \cdot \text{DM}}{\Delta m}
$$



## Feeding Rate

Usually reported in g/d.

$$
\text{FR} = \frac{m_{feed}}{\Delta t}
$$
, with $m_{feed}}$ being the total mass of feed administered between two time points $\Delta t$.



## Geometric bodyweight

$$
\text{GBW} = \sqrt{m_{start} \cdot m_{end}}
$$


## Metabolic bodyweight

$$
\text{MBW} 
  = \text{GBW}^{0.8} 
  = \sqrt{m_{start} \cdot m_{end}}^{0.8}
$$


## Nutrient Efficiency Ratio

$$
\text{NER} 
  = \frac{\Delta m}{\text{FI} \cdot \gamma_{x} \cdot \text{DM}_{feed}}
$$
, with $\gamma_{x}$ denoting the mass fraction of a nutrient $x$ in the feed.




## Relative Growth

$$
\Delta m_{rel}
  = \frac{m_{\text{end}} - m_{\text{init}}}{m_{end}}
$$



## Relative Growth Rate

$$
\text{RGR}
  = \frac{\Delta m}{\Delta t \cdot \sqrt{m_{end} \cdot m_{start}}}
$$


## Specific Growth Rate

Also called Instantaneous Growth Rate.

$$
\text{SGR} 
  = \frac{\ln {m_{\text{end}} } - \ln {m_{\text{init}}} }{\Delta t}
  = \frac{\ln \frac{m_{\text{end}}}{m_{\text{init}}}} {\Delta t}
$$


## Thermal Growth Coefficient

$$
\text{TGC} = 
  \frac{\sqrt[3]{m_{\text{end}}} - \sqrt[3]{m_{\text{init}}}}{\sum_1^t T \cdot t} \cdot 1000
$$
